title: affinity-driven-kv-microshards-with-late-binding-for-multi-gpu-topologies
creator: Ava Chen
description: We need a low-latency, memory-efficient KV cache sharding strategy that works across heterogeneous multi-GPU topologies and cooperates with tensor and pipeline parallelism. This ticket proposes affinity-driven microshards with late-binding allocation and epochal compaction to reduce cross-GPU traffic during hot-key access patterns while keeping continuous batching latency predictable.
background: Current slab/striping approaches reduce worst-case memory pressure but cause unnecessary cross-GPU fetches for short-lived hot sequences and interact poorly with pipeline-parallel layout changes. Continuous batching increases KV reuse but amplifies the cost of misaligned shard ownership when tensor/pipeline placement shifts. Prior work (ENG-7420, ENG-25681, ENG-30765) explored coarse striping and KV spill; this design is focused on microshard affinity and runtime binding to the serving pipeline that minimizes remote transfers and enables incremental compaction without full-model pauses.
proposed_solution: Create a fine-grained microshard layer (4-16MB microshards) that are allocated with an affinity score to GPUs based on recent access locality, model slice ownership (tensor parallel shards), and pipeline stage placement. Allocation is late-bound at request enqueue time: a microshard may be logically owned by a GPU but physically migrated or shadowed to the executor GPU when the request’s compute stages differ. We introduce epochal compaction windows where lightly-used microshards are compacted/merged and migrated during low-SLO load, with background prefetch hints driven by continuous-batching traces. The runtime exposes a placement policy and a cost model used by the router to choose which GPU to schedule the request on to avoid remote KV fetches when possible.
implementation_steps: 1) Prototype microshard metadata and affinity scorer (locality + tensor/pipeline co-ownership) in runtime metadata store
2) Add late-binding allocator hook at enqueue where request’s expected compute stages are annotated and candidate GPU placement selected
3) Implement shadow-copy mechanism to create transient local copy of microshard for hot short-lived sequences with explicit TTL and ref-counting
4) Build epochal compaction background worker that merges low-use microshards and schedules migration during slack windows
5) Integrate prefetch hint generator from continuous-batching traces and KV access heatmaps
6) Add metrics/tracing and end-to-end load tests including multi-topology (2xA100 + 4xH100 mixed) scenarios
7) Run staged rollout behind a config flag and compare against current slab striping baseline
acceptance_criteria: p95 generation latency regression <= 5ms vs baseline under typical PLG load
remote-KV-fetch rate reduced by >= 30% on hot-sequence workloads
GPU memory fragmentation (free-block-count metric) improved or unchanged after epochal compaction
No increase in tail OOM events in mixed topology canary (same workload)
Circuit-breaker exists to fall back to current slab/striping strategy
risks: prefetching/migration could increase PCIe/NVLink traffic and harm latency if mis-tuned
affinity decisions may conflict with autoscaler placement leading to suboptimal packing
complexity of ref-counted shadow copies increases memory accounting bugs
epochal compaction windows may not align with real traffic patterns causing wasted work
testing_plan: unit tests for affinity scorer and allocator decisions
simulator to replay continuous-batching traces and measure predicted vs actual remote fetches
canary against existing runtime on dedicated pool with synthetic hot-key traces
stress test across topology permutations and pipeline/tensor parallel reconfiguration
A/B experiment in production traffic for a small tenant group with rollback automation
